summary: Tested the new 'Standard-Logo + improved logo scaling' feature set end-to-end. Backend: new pytest suite (15 tests) for logo_scale bounds (0.5-7.0 accepted, 7.5/8/0.4/0/-1 -> 422), persistence via GET, auth requirement (401), static SVG delivery (both /logo-standard.svg and /logo-standard-light.svg return 200 + image/svg+xml), /api/media/info shape and no _id leak — 15/15 passed. Frontend (Playwright, 1920/768/390): navbar shows the standard SVG (no text wordmark) at exactly 60px height with logo_scale=1.5; footer and open mobile menu correctly use the light variant; Admin > Medien 'Standard-Logo' card shows both variants with correct backgrounds and download links (href + download attribute); slider reaches 50% and 700% with correct percentage readout and live preview scaling; INSTANT-APPLY verified: saving 300% then SPA-navigating to '/' without reload immediately rendered the navbar logo at 120px (style height:120px); persistence after full reload confirmed; mobile 390px capped at 44px, tablet 768px at 56px, no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth=390/768), menu toggle not overlapped; custom logo upload (transparent PNG) instantly appeared in navbar without reload and deletion instantly restored the standard SVG. No console errors and no >=400 responses in any flow. Cleanup done: test logo deleted, logo_scale restored to 1.5.

issues: The is capped by max-w-[420px] with object-contain, so above scale ~2.7 the artwork stops growing visually (SVG aspect 340:88 -> 420px width = ~109px visual height) while the element box keeps growing (e.g. 120px box at 300%, 280px box at 700%), adding empty vertical padding inside the header. Consequence: slider values above ~290% have virtually no visible effect on desktop and none on mobile/tablet (44/56px caps), which makes the advertised 700% range misleading. Suggest capping the slider at a value that is actually effective on desktop or using width-based scaling.
At the 44px height cap the 'GEBÄUDEREINIGUNG' sub-line of the standard SVG renders ~4px tall and is barely legible; consider a compact mobile logo variant (drop icon + CLEANORA only).

action_items: Optional: reconsider effective max slider value / scaling model — desktop visual height saturates at ~109px because of max-w-[420px]; 300%-700% look nearly identical.
Optional: compact standard-logo variant for mobile (sub-line unreadable at 44px cap).
critical_code_review_comments: LogoScale.save() PUTs {...cfg, logo_scale} where cfg comes from GET /site-settings — safe today, but any extra read-only field added to that response would be echoed back into the update payload; prefer sending an explicit whitelist of fields.

Logo height is computed as 40 * logo_scale in two places (Logo.jsx and AdminDashboard LogoScale preview) — extract the 40px base + cap logic into one shared helper so admin preview and site rendering can never diverge (they already diverge: the admin preview has no mobile caps and no 420px width cap).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 13 requested feature checks passed

seed_data_creation: Temporary transparent PNG /tmp/TEST_logo.png uploaded as custom logo, then deleted; logo_scale temporarily set to 0.5/3/7 and restored to 1.5.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New suite: /app/backend/tests/test_logo_scale.py (bounds/persistence/static SVG). Correct admin testids: admin-tab-media, media-logo-input/upload/delete (NOT media-file-logo), logo-scale-slider/value/save/preview, standard-logo-dark/light + standard-logo-download-dark/light. Use scoped selectors for the logo image: '[data-testid="main-nav"] [data-testid="logo-link"] img' and '[data-testid="site-footer"] ...' — the plain testid matches 2 elements (strict-mode violation). Instant-apply can be exercised with history.pushState + popstate to simulate SPA navigation without reload. State left clean: no custom logo, logo_scale=1.5.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect found. The only deviation from the stated expectation is cosmetic: at 300% the navbar image box is 120px as designed, but the visible artwork is ~109px tall because the desktop width cap (max-w-[420px]) plus object-contain letterboxes the 340x88 SVG.
